culture.name: Philippines
culture.language: Filipino, English, Cebuano, Ilocano or your home language
culture.timeDifference: It is already tomorrow morning there.
culture.homeTravelNote: a long flight across the Pacific, half a day in the air

cookLines: Chicken simmers in soy sauce, vinegar, garlic and bay leaves, and the whole apartment smells like home.
You taste the sauce and let it cook down a little longer, the way your mother would.
{roommate} wanders in and asks what smells so good.
You share it at the counter over hot rice, spooning the sauce on until the pot is clean.

festivals.title: Christmas, far from home
festivals.body: At home Christmas begins long before December, with star lanterns in every window, dawn Masses and the whole family at the table for Noche Buena. Campus is quiet and cold.
festivals.join: Spend Christmas Eve with a Filipino family from church or the association.
festivals.joinText: There is a parol in the window, a table that keeps filling up and karaoke after midnight. A tita you met once sends you home with enough food for a week.
festivals.host: Host a Noche Buena for students who could not travel.
festivals.hostText: You make pancit and someone brings leche flan. At midnight everyone calls home at once, and the room fills with a dozen families' voices.
festivals.skip: Call home during Noche Buena and go to bed.
festivals.skipText: It is still morning for you and already midnight for them. Your cousins crowd the screen to greet you, and you feel close to it all.

festivals.title: Holy Week
festivals.body: Holy Week falls in the middle of the term this year. At home the country slows down, offices close and many families go back to their home province.
festivals.join: Go to Easter service with Filipino friends and eat together afterward.
festivals.joinText: The potluck after the service covers three tables. Someone's lola asks which province your family is from, and it turns out she knows your town.
festivals.host: Cook a quiet meal for friends on Easter Sunday.
festivals.hostText: You keep it simple and take your time. Your friends ask what the week is like at home, and you find you have a lot to say.
festivals.skip: Call your family and spend the weekend resting.
festivals.skipText: Your mother tells you who came home this year and who could not. You promise to be there for the next one.

festivals.title: Independence Day, 12 June
festivals.body: At home there are flag ceremonies and a public holiday for Araw ng Kalayaan. Here it is an ordinary summer weekday.
festivals.join: Go to the Filipino community's Independence Day picnic.
festivals.joinText: There are flags on every table, a line for lumpia and barbecue, and children running everywhere. You stay until the last song.
festivals.host: Cook for friends and put a small flag on the table.
festivals.hostText: Your friends try sinigang for the first time and ask for seconds. Someone asks what the sun and stars on the flag mean, and you tell them.
festivals.skip: Send greetings to the family group chat and get on with your day.
festivals.skipText: Your phone fills with flags and photos from home. You smile at every one.

familyCall: It is morning in Manila when you call at night, twelve to sixteen hours ahead of you.
Your mother asks if you have eaten, and whether it is very cold where you are.
Your father asks about your classes, then your lola takes the phone to give you her blessing.
They are starting their day as you end yours, and you fall asleep a little lighter.
culture.homeMoneyNote: Money from home is converted from pesos, and every swing in the exchange rate shows up in your account.
culture.familySupportNote: Designed at the India baseline of 1.0. This research found no sourced figure that would justify more or less family support for Filipino students, so the factor is left unchanged.

entryNotes.F1: About 4,573 students from the Philippines studied in the US in 2024/25, and Filipino nationals received 1,020 F-1 visas in FY2024.
entryNotes.H1B: Filipino nationals received 3,565 H-1B visas in FY2024, and the Philippines has its own EB-3 green card date, 15 August 2023 in the November 2026 bulletin.
entryNotes.B2: The Philippines is not in the Visa Waiver Program, so every visitor needs a B visa before travelling.
entryNotes.O1: The O-1 has no lottery or country limit, and the EB-1 green card that often follows is current for Filipino applicants in the November 2026 bulletin.
entryNotes.FAM: The Philippines has its own family queue, among the longest: in November 2026 sibling petitions filed before 15 May 2008 are being processed, and the Philippines is not eligible for the Diversity Visa lottery.
entryNotes.EWI: CBP counts Filipino nationals as a separate group in its border encounter data, and entering without inspection usually blocks a green card from inside the US later.
entryNotes.ASY: In FY2024 EOIR reported fewer than four asylum grants and 11 denials for Filipino nationals, too few to give a rate.

facts.title: Time difference to Manila
facts.text: The Philippines is on Philippine Standard Time, UTC+8, with no daylight saving. It is 13 hours ahead of US Eastern in winter and 12 in summer, and 16 hours ahead of Pacific in winter and 15 in summer.

facts.title: Round-trip flight, Philippines to US
facts.text: Design estimate of $1,400. No sourced fare was found; real prices change a great deal with season and route.

facts.title: F-1 visas issued to Filipinos
facts.text: Filipino nationals received 1,020 F-1 visas in FY2024, down from a peak of 1,237 in FY2022, and 777 in FY2025. Figures are State Department data republished by VisaGrader.

facts.title: Filipino students in the US
facts.text: Open Doors counted 4,573 students from the Philippines in US higher education in 2024/25, up about 12 percent from 4,100, the 32nd largest group.

facts.title: Remittances to the Philippines
facts.text: Central bank data put cash remittances from overseas Filipinos at a record $35.63 billion in 2025, up 3.3 percent from $34.49 billion in 2024. The United States was the largest source, at 39.7 percent.

facts.title: H-1B visas for Filipinos
facts.text: Filipino nationals received 3,565 H-1B visas in FY2024 and 3,350 in FY2025, up from 1,217 in FY2018. The Philippines' share of all H-1B approvals was not found in an official table.

facts.title: Asylum decisions for Filipino applicants
facts.text: In FY2024 EOIR reported fewer than four asylum grants and 11 denials for Filipino nationals, with 151 cases not adjudicated. The numbers are too small to give a rate.

facts.title: Green card queues for the Philippines
facts.text: The Philippines has its own column in the visa bulletin. November 2026 final action dates as transcribed by law firms: F1 1 Nov 2013, F3 22 Jul 2006, F4 (siblings) 15 May 2008; EB-1 current, EB-2 1 Apr 2025, EB-3 15 Aug 2023.

mechanics.ebDates: November 2026 Visa Bulletin final action dates for the Philippines: EB-1 current, EB-2 1 April 2025 (same as Rest of World), EB-3 15 August 2023 (law firm transcription, LIKELY, https://www.gozellaw.com/blog/november-2026-visa-bulletin).
mechanics.asylumNote: Null because EOIR suppressed the grant count (fewer than four) for the Philippines in FY2024; 11 denials, 8 abandoned, 151 not adjudicated. https://www.justice.gov/eoir/media/1344846/dl
